message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | State at STP | Gas |
| | Molar mass | 1.008 g mol⁻¹ (¹H) |
| **Physical Properties** | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (20.3 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas, 25 °C) | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ g⁻¹ |
| | Refractive index (visible light) | 1.000132 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H₂) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Dipole moment (H₂) | 0 (homonuclear diatomic) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.7928 µB (proton) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a proton donor (H⁺) in aqueous solution |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) |
| | Redox behavior | Strong reducing agent (especially in metal hydrides) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | H₂O, HF, NH₃ exhibit H‑bonding; H₂ itself does not |
| | Solubility in water | 0.0006 g g⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Variable; generally low in non‑polar solvents |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 0.015% natural abundance |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion & radiolabeling |
| **Applications** | Fuel cell fuel | H₂ + O₂ → H₂O (electricity) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid H₂ + liquid O₂ |
| | Metallurgy | Hydrogen embrittlement, annealing |
| | Chemical synthesis | Hydride reagents, hydrogenation |
| | Medical imaging | ¹H MRI (proton imaging) |
| | Fusion research | D‑T fusion (tritium + deuterium) |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability range (air) | 4–75 % (v/v) |
| | Explosion limit | 4 % (lower) – 75 % (upper) |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic; high pressure can cause asphyxiation |
| | Storage | Cryogenic tanks (liquid) or high‑pressure cylinders (gas) |
| | Environmental impact | Low; combustion produces only water |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Hydrogen is the simplest element**: one proton, one electron, and (in its most common form) one neutron.
- **It exists mainly as a diatomic gas (H₂)** under normal conditions, but it also forms a wide variety of compounds.
- **Its isotopes** (protium, deuterium, tritium) have distinct nuclear properties that make them useful in scientific research and industry.
- **Physically**, hydrogen is extremely light, has a very low boiling point, and is highly flammable.
- **Chemically**, it behaves as both an acid (donating H⁺) and a base (forming hydrides), and it is a powerful reducing agent.
- **Technologically**, hydrogen is central to fuel cells, rocket propulsion, and potential fusion energy, while its proton signal is the basis of MRI imaging.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
